# vgi4bio

<!-- badges: start -->
[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/337747952.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23735309)
<!-- badges: end -->

The package vgi4bio contains functions to estimate relative species abundances from opportunistic records, using the data combination methods of Giraud et al. (2016, *Biometrics*, [doi:10.1111/biom.12431](https://doi.org/10.1111/biom.12431)). It also implements the Bayesian model of Coron et al. (2018, *Environmental and Ecological Statistics*, [doi:10.1007/s10651-018-0398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10651-018-0398-2)), which additionally estimates the habitat preferences of the species and of the observers (requires [JAGS](https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io) and the R package `rjags`, or the R packages `nimble` and `nimbleHMC`).

## Context

This package was developed within the ANR project **VGI4BIO**, whose aim is to provide generic and reproducible tools to estimate trends in spatial distributions from opportunistic data, for a possible integration into the Galaxy platform (Galaxy-E). The Galaxy integration has not been done yet.

## Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fun_abund_estim()` | Fit the model of Giraud et al. (2016) (quasi-Poisson GLM combining standardized and opportunistic counts) |
| `fun_abund_hab_estim()` | Fit the Bayesian model of Coron et al. (2018), with habitat preferences of species and observers (JAGS or nimble HMC) |
| `fun_rel_abund()` | Extract the relative abundance of each species on each site, with confidence or credible intervals |
| `fun_hab_pref()` | Extract the habitat preferences of species and observers (Coron et al. model) |
| `fun_pred_std()` | Predict the counts of an independent standardized survey (model validation) |
| `fun_pearsons()`, `fun_braycurt()` | Compare estimated and reference abundances (Pearson correlation, Bray-Curtis dissimilarity) |
| `fun_simul_hab()` | Simulate data following the design of Coron et al. (2018) |

The data set `Aquitaine` contains the bird counts used by Giraud et al. (2016). The script `inst/scripts/reproduce_coron2018.R` reproduces Table 1 of Coron et al. (2018) from the authors' data files, which are not distributed with the package.

## Documentation

To have an overview of the package, read the vignettes after installing the package by:

``` {r, eval=F}
vignette("tutorial", package = "vgi4bio")   # Giraud et al. (2016)
vignette("habitat", package = "vgi4bio")    # Coron et al. (2018)
```


## Installing *vgi4bio*

To install the development version from GitHub (with the vignette):

1. Install the release version of devtools from CRAN with install.packages("devtools").

2. Make sure you have a working development environment.

- Windows: Install Rtools.
- Mac: Install Xcode from the Mac App Store.
- Linux: Install a compiler and various development libraries (details vary across different flavors of Linux).

Then:

``` {r, eval=F}
library(devtools)
install_github("KarinePrince/vgi4bio", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The Bayesian model of Coron et al. (2018) requires either [JAGS](https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io) (to be installed separately) and the R package `rjags`, or the R packages `nimble` and `nimbleHMC` (recommended, much faster convergence; a C++ compiler is needed):

``` {r, eval=F}
install.packages("rjags")                      # after installing JAGS
install.packages(c("nimble", "nimbleHMC"))
```

The package is not (yet) available on CRAN.
  
Once installed, the package can be loaded using:  

``` {r, eval=F}
library(vgi4bio)
```

## Citation

To cite the package and the papers describing the models:

``` {r, eval=F}
citation("vgi4bio")
```

*The package requires R >= 3.5.*
